ei.title: Why Researchers Choose the Path of Science
ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: Scientific research is hard. Reaching the stage of becoming an independent and productive researcher able to pursue one's interests requires a long period of study followed by more years of apprenticeship. Even after that it requires long hours and often repetitive detailed work with little chance of obtaining wealth and glory, except for a tiny number who obtain Nobel prizes and the like, and even for them the fame is often short-lived. The respect and approval of the small community of their peers is often their main reward. So why do they do it? Almost all do it because of an intense curiosity, the desire to understand how the world works. Many because it promises to be able to solve important problems and make the world a better place. Yet others go into it because it is intellectually stimulating and rewarding, and has the promise of prestige, a good career, and a modestly comfortable lifestyle. When it comes to individual scientists, there will likely be a range of overlapping motivations for their choice.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
Many because it promises to be able to __________ and make the world a better place. → 세상을 더 나은 곳으로 만들겠다는 동기와 병렬로, '중요한 문제를 해결한다'가 적절

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.analysis:
① 부와 명예를 쉽게 → little chance of obtaining wealth and glory = 불일치

① 최고의 영예를 받더라도 대중의 관심은 금방 사라진다 → 양보의 핵심 함축 ←정답

② 과학적 발견의 가치 상실 → 발견의 가치가 아니라 명성의 일시성

③ 은퇴 후 잊힘 → 은퇴 언급 없음

④ 다른 분야보다 지속적 → 반대 의미
det.tip: even for them(양보) + short-lived → 최고 영예도 일시적

ch: 최고의 영예를 받더라도 대중의 관심은 금방 사라진다.
과학적 발견은 시간이 지나면 가치를 잃는다.
과학 연구의 명성은 다른 분야보다 지속적이다.

questions.passage: Scientific research is hard. Reaching the stage of becoming an independent and productive researcher able to pursue one's interests requires a long period of study followed by more years of apprenticeship. Even after that it requires long hours and often repetitive detailed work with little chance of obtaining wealth and glory, except for a tiny number who obtain Nobel prizes and the like, and even for them the fame is often short-lived. The respect and approval of the small community of their peers is often their main reward. So why do <u>they</u> do it? Almost all do it because of an intense curiosity, the desire to understand how the world works. Many because it promises to be able to solve important problems and make the world a better place. Yet others go into it because it is intellectually stimulating and rewarding, and has the promise of prestige, a good career, and a modestly comfortable lifestyle. When it comes to individual scientists, there will likely be a range of overlapping motivations for their choice.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 they가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
So why do they do it? 문맥에서 they는 앞에서 설명한 과학 연구를 수행하는 사람들(연구자들 전체)을 지칭. 노벨상 수상자는 극소수이고, 교수나 동료는 별도로 언급되지 않음.

① 노벨상 수상자들 → a tiny number에 해당, 전체 아님
② 교수들 → 언급 없음
③ 과학 연구에 종사하는 사람들 → 글 전체의 주어 ←정답
④ 평가하는 동료들 → peers는 보상을 주는 측
det.tip: they = 글의 주제인 과학 연구자 전체
